headline: Cyclone Akvan heads for the Andhra coast, Nvidia's CEO drama shakes the AI industry, and a third US aircraft carrier reaches the Middle East.

stories.title: Cyclone Akvan to hit Andhra Pradesh coast on November 20
stories.summary: The weather department says Cyclone Akvan will cross the Andhra coast between Nellore and Tuni by noon on November 20. Chief Minister Naidu reviewed preparations, and 173 fishing boats have not yet returned.
stories.why_it_matters: Coastal Andhra faces heavy rain and wind, and farmers are being told to harvest and move crops to safety.

stories.title: Cyclone Akvan may bring heavy rain to Telangana from November 19 to 21
stories.summary: Four Telangana districts are under an orange alert for heavy to very heavy rain on November 20. The effects may begin on Thursday, November 19.
stories.why_it_matters: Heavy rain could disrupt travel and daily life across Telangana.

stories.title: Third US aircraft carrier arrives in the Middle East amid Iran tensions
stories.summary: The USS Theodore Roosevelt has joined two other US carriers in the region. Reports ask whether the US-Iran war could resume.
stories.why_it_matters: A renewed war could push up oil prices and hurt global markets.

stories.title: Russia stalls Ukraine peace talks and proposes separate non-attack deals with European countries
stories.summary: Russia has offered non-aggression pacts to individual nations, a move that could weaken NATO's shared defence promise. Peace talks on Ukraine remain stuck.
stories.why_it_matters: It signals the Ukraine war is not ending soon and that Europe's security alliance is under pressure.

stories.title: Rupee strengthens as foreign money flows into Indian shares
stories.summary: The rupee closed 0.3% higher at 93.92 to the dollar. Foreign investors put nearly $10 billion into Indian shares in November, and the Nifty 50 rose 0.6%.
stories.why_it_matters: Steady foreign inflows support the market where your SIP money is invested.

stories.title: Sebi may let foreign investors hold bigger stakes before extra disclosure rules apply
stories.summary: Sebi, India's market regulator, is considering raising the ownership limit for foreign portfolio investors from 10% to 25%. A consultation paper will be released soon.
stories.why_it_matters: Easier rules could attract more foreign money into Indian markets.

stories.title: Mahanadi Coalfields IPO opens November 19
stories.summary: Coal India is selling shares in its subsidiary Mahanadi Coalfields in an ₹8,981-crore offer. The price band is ₹129 to ₹136 per share, and one retail lot of 110 shares costs ₹14,960.
stories.why_it_matters: It is a large public issue from a government-owned coal company.

stories.title: Nvidia in turmoil after CEO Jensen Huang resigns over spy scandal
stories.summary: Nvidia's co-founder Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO after a scandal involving a suspected Chinese spy, and there are rumours he may try to return. US lawmakers from both parties want tighter limits on exporting AI chips and want Nvidia's leaders to testify.
stories.why_it_matters: Nvidia is central to the AI boom, so its leadership crisis affects the whole tech industry and markets.

stories.title: Alibaba launches new flagship AI model Qwen4-Max
stories.summary: China's Alibaba unveiled Qwen4-Max, saying it handles complex professional and scientific work better and has stronger safety protections. It was among the most discussed items on Hacker News.
stories.why_it_matters: It shows Chinese AI models keeping pace with the best from the US.

stories.title: IBM CEO says AI could replace 10-20% of jobs in a decade
stories.summary: IBM's CEO Arvind Krishna said call-centre and back-office (BPO) work will likely see the biggest cuts. IBM also plans to invest $3 billion a year in India.
stories.why_it_matters: It is a direct warning about job changes in India's outsourcing industry, along with a sign of continued big-tech investment here.

stories.title: Jay Shah re-elected ICC chairman for a second term
stories.summary: The former BCCI secretary was the only candidate in the running for the role.
stories.why_it_matters: India's cricket administrators keep control of the sport's global governing body.
